advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or bound with a best-effort ls-remote) that build-stale measures against the local, un-fetched origin/main and therefore understates drift on a repo that has not fetched.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/doctor_build_freshness.py: `tracked_full = resolve_commit(TRACKED_REF, repo_root)` with `TRACKED_REF = "origin/main"` and no fetch performed

detect_drift docstring in build_drift.py notes drift is measured against whatever the local checkout last fetched; ticket comment records the same as a carried advisory: 'build_drift.detect_drift performs no fetch, so origin/main is whatever the local checkout last fetched -- a checkout that has not fetched recently UNDERSTATES drift.'
advisory.finding: The build-stale signal compares the published build against a hardcoded local `origin/main` ref (TRACKED_REF) without any fetch, so on a source repo whose `origin/main` is itself stale the measured 'commits behind' is understated and a genuinely stale build can read OK — the check's healthy verdict is indistinguishable from a repo that simply has not fetched.
